name: janetmalzahn/llm-phacking
why: Replication archive for R5. Borrow: its prompt matrix (2 framings x 4 nudges x 10 runs) is a ready red-team test for our study agent; every run keeps its R script and session log; specification counts come from an LLM counter cross-checked against a second model (haiku_sonnet_comparison.csv)

name: zachrewolinski/stat-genie
why: Code for R4: perturbation and null-shuffle sanity checks run through the Codex CLI on BLADE datasets; borrow the idea of a null arm that needs no agent self-report, but no license so read only

name: nbreznau/CRI
why: Data and workflow of R11 (73 teams): numbered literate notebooks with rendered HTML beside each, relative paths, Binder runtime pinned to a package snapshot; a model for our replicate.ipynb and for logging every team's decisions

name: behavioral-data/BLADE
why: Benchmark whose ground truth is the analysis decisions (constructs, transforms, models) of independent expert analysts, built from many-analyst studies incl. the soccer data; README says a hold-out test set is still pending; candidate known-answer tasks for new-study

name: uwdata/boba
why: Multiverse DSL: one template script plus a JSON of decision points compiles every universe, runs them all and merges outputs into one table; borrow for the multiverse arm of the study grader; last push 2021 so check it still runs

name: MUCollective/multiverse
why: R package that declares alternative analysis branches at each decision point and returns every outcome; GPL-3.0 so use as a reference or external tool, do not copy into the plugin

name: masurp/specr
why: R specification-curve package (define, run and plot all specifications); GPL-3.0 so tool not copy source; pairs with the specification-curve figures in R1

name: aeturrell/specification_curve
why: Python specification-curve package, actively pushed; no detected license so read only; its API shows what a study agent should emit (all specifications, not one)

name: ml-preregister/preregistration-template
why: Two-form markdown preregistration for predictive modelling (form A at start, form B before model testing) timestamped by git history, the same mechanism as our PREREG.md commit; borrow the A/B split and read the linked Hofman et al. preprint

name: codecheckers/codecheck
why: CODECHECK process: an independent person re-runs the authors' code, lists the reproduced outputs in a manifest (codecheck.yml) and issues a certificate; the model for our independent re-execution gate (README says MIT but gh reports NOASSERTION, check the raw LICENSE before copying)

name: codecheckers/register
why: Public register of CODECHECK certificates; shows how independent reproduction results are logged and published; borrow the register idea for benchmark scorecards

name: the-turing-way/the-turing-way
why: Community handbook on reproducible, ethical, collaborative data science; chapters and checklists to mine for the new-study checklist; licence unclear per gh so cite rather than copy
